newsitem.title: SWEDEN: P&U stuns with fresh profit warning.
newsitem.headline: P&U stuns with fresh profit warning.

text.p: Swedish/U.S. drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn on Wednesday stunned the market with yet another profits warning, sending its shares plunging and forcing analysts to downgrade profit forecasts.
P&U said in a statement that sales fell by six percent in the first quarter of 1997 and earnings per share before non-recurring items were expected to drop by around 16 percent.
The group's shares ended 39 crowns lower and were down 4-3/8 to 30-1/2 in early U.S. trade.
Analysts said this was the fourth profit warning from the group since October 1996. It came just six days before the company announces the first quarter earnings.
"They have a serious credibility problem," said one analyst.

Birgit Kullhoff of the UBS pharmaceuticals team said that she would cut her earnings per share forecast by some 10 percent to around the 1996 level of $1.90. "It was a profit warning and it was unexpected," she said.
P&U said the first quarter sales shortfall was due to adverse exchange rate movements and customer inventory adjustments after a strong final quarter in 1996.
Weaker demand in Europe, particularly Germany and Sweden, and generic competition in the U.S. also ate into sales.
Chief financial officer Bob Salisbury told journalists on a telephone conference call that some of the negative factors seen hitting the first quarter were not expected to continue.
"Some of the factors will moderate and not have as adverse an effect on results in following quarters," Salisbury said.
However he declined to give forecasts for the rest of the year. "We don't give detailed forecasts," he said. "There is still a fair amount of uncertainty."
"I think that most analysts will be looking to downgrade their profit expectations," Jan Dworsky of London-based C.I. Nordic Securities.
The markets have been unpleasantly surprised several times in the past by P&U, formed in November 1995 by a merger between Michigan-based Upjohn and Sweden's Pharmacia.
An analyst from a London-based securities house said P&U's problem was that its product portfolio was too mature and it needed to throw its weight behind new products.
"The problem is that there are not too many new products," he said.
"Given that this is the fourth profit warning it is not a one-off," the analyst said. "I just hope it is the last."
